homepage.title: Can You Pass This Chef Entrance Exam?
homepage.summary: Can you control the prep, timing, ratios, and communication when service heats up?
homepage.thumbnailAlt: Chef hat above a copper pan for a fictional kitchen skills challenge

landing.quickStartText: The first prep jobs look easy. Then every timer and ticket starts to matter.

footer.aboutText: This fictional, worldwide-friendly challenge uses plain kitchen language, metric quantities, and self-contained workplace rules to explore preparation, ingredient detail, timing, ratios, communication, hygiene judgment, and calm problem-solving. It is for entertainment only and is not culinary education, food-safety guidance, professional training, certification, recruitment screening, or an official chef assessment.

stageGroups.title: Mise en Place
stageGroups.encouragement: Prep bench ready. Now prove you can spot the ingredient detail that changes the whole order.

questions.prompt: Prep list: wash herbs, portion rice, label sauces, slice bread. Which task is listed third?
questions.explanation: Label sauces is the third item in the stated prep order.

questions.prompt: Service starts at 18:00. Prep takes 45 minutes. What is the latest start time?
questions.explanation: Forty-five minutes before 18:00 is 17:15.

questions.prompt: Station list: knife, board, bowl, whisk. The bowl is ready; the knife and board are ready. What is missing?
questions.explanation: The whisk is the only listed item not accounted for.

questions.prompt: Rule: complete cold prep before hot prep. Which order follows it?
questions.explanation: The stated rule requires the cold task to be completed first.

questions.prompt: Four trays need labels. Three are labeled. What remains?
questions.explanation: Four required minus three completed leaves one tray to label.

questions.prompt: The prep card changes ‘dice onions’ to ‘slice onions.’ Which instruction should the updated plan use?
questions.explanation: The updated prep card replaces dicing with slicing.

questions.prompt: A sealed container is marked ‘for evening service.’ When is it assigned for use?
questions.explanation: The label directly states the intended service period.

stageGroups.title: Ingredient Eye
stageGroups.encouragement: Details caught. Next, control several timers without letting the kitchen control you.

questions.prompt: Recipe card: tomato, lentils, cumin, lemon. Which ingredient is not listed?
questions.explanation: Ginger does not appear on the four-item recipe card.

questions.prompt: Order A says ‘no nuts’; Order B says ‘extra nuts.’ Which detail separates the orders?
questions.explanation: The two orders give opposite instructions about nuts.

questions.prompt: Jar labels read SALT, SUGAR, FLOUR, SALT. Which label appears twice?
questions.explanation: SALT appears on the first and fourth jars.

questions.prompt: A ticket changes 2 portions to 5 portions. What changed?
questions.explanation: Only the number of portions is stated to change.

questions.prompt: Two bottles look alike. One label says vinegar; the other says oil. What should guide the choice?
questions.explanation: The label provides the relevant identity; appearance and position do not.

questions.prompt: The stock note says 6 lemons. Two are used. How many remain?
questions.explanation: Six minus two leaves four lemons.

questions.prompt: A plate guide shows sauce left, grains center, vegetables right. Where do the grains go?
questions.explanation: The plate guide explicitly places grains in the center.

stageGroups.title: Timing & Heat
stageGroups.encouragement: Timers aligned. Ratios now scale up, down, and sideways.

questions.prompt: A tray enters at 12:20 for 25 minutes. When is its timer due?
questions.explanation: Adding 25 minutes to 12:20 gives 12:45.

questions.prompt: Timer A has 8 minutes left; Timer B has 3. Which finishes first?
questions.explanation: Three minutes is less than eight, so Timer B finishes first.

questions.prompt: A sauce rests for 6 minutes after 14:32. When does the rest end?
questions.explanation: Six minutes after 14:32 is 14:38.

questions.prompt: The fictional heat dial moves from level 3 to level 5. By how many levels did it increase?
questions.explanation: The change from three to five is an increase of two.

questions.prompt: Task A takes 12 minutes and Task B starts immediately after for 7 minutes. What is the total time?
questions.explanation: Twelve plus seven gives nineteen minutes.

questions.prompt: Service is at 19:10. Final plating needs 9 minutes. When should plating begin?
questions.explanation: Nine minutes before 19:10 is 19:01.

questions.prompt: Timers repeat every 10 minutes: 16:00, 16:10, 16:20. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The sequence advances in ten-minute intervals.

stageGroups.title: Ratio Control
stageGroups.encouragement: Quantities balanced. Now keep a stack of orders moving in the right sequence.

questions.prompt: A recipe uses 200 g of rice for 2 portions. How much is needed for 4 equal portions?
questions.explanation: Doubling the portions doubles 200 g to 400 g.

questions.prompt: Three plates each need 40 g of vegetables. What is the total?
questions.explanation: Three groups of 40 g equal 120 g.

questions.prompt: A mix uses 1 part syrup to 3 parts water. How many total parts are in the mix?
questions.explanation: One syrup part plus three water parts makes four total parts.

questions.prompt: A 600 ml batch is divided equally into 3 containers. How much goes in each?
questions.explanation: Six hundred divided by three equals 200 ml.

questions.prompt: A recipe for 6 uses 12 tomatoes. At the same ratio, how many tomatoes serve 3?
questions.explanation: Halving the servings halves twelve tomatoes to six.

questions.prompt: You have 1,000 g of flour and use 350 g. How much remains?
questions.explanation: One thousand minus 350 equals 650 g.

questions.prompt: Five identical bowls share 750 ml equally. How much goes into each bowl?
questions.explanation: Seven hundred fifty divided by five equals 150 ml.

stageGroups.title: Order Flow
stageGroups.encouragement: Tickets organized. Next, make every kitchen message short, precise, and usable.

questions.prompt: Ticket order: Table 2 first, then Takeaway A, then Table 7. What comes second?
questions.explanation: Takeaway A sits between the two table tickets.

questions.prompt: Two dishes share one final garnish. Dish A is due in 4 minutes; Dish B in 9. Which needs the garnish first?
questions.explanation: Dish A has the earlier due time.

questions.prompt: Rule: cold dishes may plate while hot dishes cook. Which plan uses the waiting time?
choices: Plate the cold dish while the hot dish cooks
questions.explanation: The plan follows the stated rule and uses otherwise idle time.

questions.prompt: A ticket reads starter → main → dessert. Which course follows the starter?
questions.explanation: The given sequence places the main directly after the starter.

questions.prompt: Order 18 is ready but its table number is unreadable. What should happen before it leaves the pass?
questions.explanation: The destination must be confirmed to route the order correctly.

questions.prompt: Three identical soups are due together. How many bowls should the station prepare?
questions.explanation: One bowl is required for each of the three soups.

questions.prompt: A new verified ticket replaces an older one for the same table. Which version guides service?
questions.explanation: The verified replacement is the current instruction for that table.

stageGroups.title: Kitchen Comms
stageGroups.encouragement: Communication clear. The next station tests hygiene choices using rules stated on every card.

questions.prompt: Which update is easiest to act on?
choices: Table 4: two mains ready in three minutes
questions.explanation: It identifies the table, quantity, course, and usable time.

questions.prompt: A shouted instruction is partly lost in noise. What is the strongest response?
choices: Ask for the key instruction again and confirm it
Repeat only the part you prefer
questions.explanation: A brief repeat-and-confirm closes the communication gap.

questions.prompt: The instruction is ‘one soup, no garnish.’ Which reply closes the loop?
questions.explanation: Repeating the critical quantity and modification confirms both were heard.

questions.prompt: Two stations think the other is plating. What should happen next?
choices: Assign the owner clearly and confirm
questions.explanation: Clear ownership prevents duplicated or missed work.

questions.prompt: A delay changes from 5 minutes to 12 minutes. What should the update include?
choices: The new 12-minute delay and affected order
questions.explanation: The current delay and its target are the facts the team can use.

questions.prompt: Which message separates fact from guess?
choices: The timer shows four minutes remaining
questions.explanation: A visible timer reading is a checkable fact; the other choices predict opinions.

questions.prompt: A teammate says they missed the latest change. What restores alignment?
choices: Give a short update and ask them to repeat their task
Repeat every event of the day
questions.explanation: A concise recap plus confirmation rebuilds the shared plan.

stageGroups.title: Hygiene Judgment
stageGroups.encouragement: Standards protected. Now solve shortages and changes without losing control of service.

questions.prompt: Fictional kitchen rule: allergen-free orders use the blue labeled tools only. Which tools should be used for that order?
questions.explanation: The self-contained kitchen rule assigns blue labeled tools to the order.

questions.prompt: A container has no identity label. What is the sensible professional response?
choices: Set it aside and follow the kitchen's checking process
questions.explanation: An unidentified ingredient should be checked through the established process, not guessed.

questions.prompt: A team member changes tasks after handling waste. What should guide the next step?
choices: Follow the kitchen's required hand-cleaning procedure
questions.explanation: The correct action is to use the workplace procedure designed for the transition.

questions.prompt: Rule: raw-prep boards and ready-to-serve boards must stay separate. Which plan follows the rule?
questions.explanation: Separate labeled boards directly satisfy the stated separation rule.

questions.prompt: A dish has been waiting beyond the kitchen's stated hold limit. What should happen?
questions.explanation: The scenario supplies a hold limit, so the stated workplace procedure should be followed.

questions.prompt: A cleaning bottle label is damaged and unreadable. What is the best first move?
choices: Remove it from use and report it through the proper process
questions.explanation: An unreadable product should not be guessed at or used until properly identified.

questions.prompt: A guest flags an allergy after the ticket was sent. What is the strongest response?
choices: Assume the original order is safe
Stop the order and activate the kitchen's allergy procedure
questions.explanation: The new information should trigger the kitchen's established allergy process immediately.

stageGroups.title: Problem Solving
stageGroups.encouragement: Problems solved. The rush now tests which fact deserves your attention first.

questions.prompt: A recipe needs 8 portions but only 6 matching plates are ready. What is the useful first fact to communicate?
questions.explanation: Eight required minus six ready leaves a shortfall of two plates.

questions.prompt: The blender is unavailable. The prep card lists an approved whisk method. What should the team use?
questions.explanation: The approved alternative is already defined on the prep card.

questions.prompt: A delivery has 18 items; the order expected 20. What is the shortage?
questions.explanation: Twenty expected minus eighteen received equals a shortage of two.

questions.prompt: One garnish runs out, and the menu card lists a verified substitute. What is the strongest response?
choices: Confirm and use the listed substitute
questions.explanation: The verified substitute provides the approved route to keep the order accurate.

questions.prompt: A plate returns because its order number is wrong. What should happen before replating?
choices: Confirm the correct ticket and identify the mismatch
questions.explanation: The source ticket and mismatch need confirmation before the correction is made.

questions.prompt: Two solutions both work, but one takes 4 minutes and one takes 9. If all other factors are equal, which is efficient?
questions.explanation: With every other factor equal, the shorter method completes the task sooner.

questions.prompt: A station is overloaded with three tasks. What is the clearest reset?
choices: List priorities, assign owners, and confirm the next action
questions.explanation: Priorities and ownership turn an overloaded station into a shared plan.

stageGroups.title: Under Pressure
stageGroups.encouragement: Rush controlled. The final service combines every prep, timing, ratio, and communication skill.

questions.prompt: A verified allergy update arrives as a routine garnish request comes in. Which needs attention first?
questions.explanation: The allergy update can materially change how the order must be handled.

questions.prompt: Two timers sound together. One order is due now; the other has a confirmed two-minute hold. Which is checked first?
questions.explanation: The stated hold creates time for the second order, while the first is already due.

questions.prompt: A ticket number changes from 68 to 86. What should happen before the dish leaves?
questions.explanation: A transposed identifier can misroute the dish and should be confirmed.

questions.prompt: The kitchen is noisy and the final instruction is unclear. What balances speed and accuracy?
choices: Pause briefly, confirm the key words, then act
questions.explanation: A focused confirmation resolves the uncertainty without abandoning the task.

questions.prompt: A new verified ticket conflicts with the old prep note. Which should guide the order?
questions.explanation: The verified current ticket supersedes the older instruction for this order.

questions.prompt: A teammate misses a step after an interruption. What is the safest recovery?
choices: Return to the last confirmed step and restate what remains
questions.explanation: Returning to a known point avoids carrying a hidden gap into service.

questions.prompt: Three dishes are ready, but only two match the table ticket. What is the strongest response?
choices: Hold the unmatched dish and verify its destination
questions.explanation: The two matching dishes are accounted for; the extra dish needs verification.

stageGroups.title: The Final Service
stageGroups.encouragement: Final service complete. Your chef profile is ready for the reveal.

questions.prompt: Final ticket: 4 portions, 150 g each. What total quantity is required?
questions.explanation: Four groups of 150 g equal 600 g.

questions.prompt: Prep begins at 17:25 and takes 35 minutes. When is it complete?
questions.explanation: Thirty-five minutes after 17:25 is 18:00.

questions.prompt: Order: no dairy, sauce on side, Table 9. Which handover preserves every key detail?
choices: No dairy for an unknown table
Table 9: no dairy, sauce on side
questions.explanation: The complete handover keeps the table, restriction, and sauce instruction together.

questions.prompt: The label says 12 portions; the verified ticket says 10. Rule: use the verified current ticket. How many should be prepared?
questions.explanation: The stated rule makes the verified current ticket controlling.

questions.prompt: A station has finished prep, confirmed tools, and checked the ticket. What is the best next move?
choices: Begin the planned task and monitor for updates
questions.explanation: With the required checks complete, the station can proceed while staying alert to change.

questions.prompt: One ingredient is uncertain and could change the order. What should happen before service?
questions.explanation: A material uncertainty should be resolved before the order is served.

questions.prompt: The quantities match, timers are clear, and all modifications are confirmed. What completes the strongest final handover?
choices: State what is ready, what is next, and who owns it
questions.explanation: A structured handover keeps status, sequence, and ownership visible to the team.
